findings: Potential WPF initialization race — Program.cs assumes App() constructor and InitializeComponent() will succeed and not reference GUI resources. If App.xaml.cs throws an exception during component initialization and a CLI arg is present, the error is caught but logs only via LogService, which may not exist if SettingsService hasn't loaded yet. The try-catch should initialize LogService first.

Null coalescing in Topshelf callbacks — ServiceManager passes null! (null-forgiving operator) to WhenStarted and WhenStopped, but Topshelf calls these with a non-null HostControl argument. While this works in practice (the parameter is not used), it silently ignores the contract and would confuse maintainers. The callback signatures should match Topshelf's expected HostControl contract or be documented.

Silent mode detection flaw — App.xaml.cs defensive check exits silently when no recognized args are present (not --gui, --scan, --send, --headless). If someone runs the app with an invalid flag or misspells an argument, the app shuts down with only a warning log, not an error, leaving no feedback to the user.
